main_text.p: Est aliquando apostrophus ex ꝏ ante ε & o in υ: ut ταρεέχω ταρϋχω, emi- neo: ταρείλαδε, ταρϋλαδε, anticipavit, prævertit: ταρεέδωκας, ταρϋδωκας, prodidifti: ταρεπῄ, ταρυπῄ, proponebat: ταρέοπλον, ταρϋπλον, prævisum: ταρεοφείλω, ταρϋφείλω, ante debeo: ταρε ὀλίγου, ταρϋλίγου, paulo ante.

head.i: Cap. 17. De præpositionum pleo- nasmo, anastrophe, & apo- strophe.

main_text.p: Præpositio sæpe cum suo compo- sito repetitur. Eucl. ἐαν ἀπὸ ἴσων ἴσα ἀ- φαιρεθῇ, τὰ καταλειπόμενα ἴσα ἐστίν, si ab æqualibus æqualia ablata sint, reliqua sunt æqualia. Xenophon, ὥσπερ ἐν ἵπ- ποις, ἕτω ἡ ἐν αἰ ἀνθρώποις τῶν ἐγγίγνεται, ut in equis, ita & in hominibus quibuf- dam ingeneratur. Item, ὥσπερ βασιλεῖ συ- στρατεύεσθαι, cum rege commilitare.

page.notes: Greek words in the scan are printed in a heavily accented, partly worn state; the Greek transcriptions above are approximate and several accents and letters are uncertain. The phrase "ταρϋ..." forms with the preposition ꝏ (παρά, shown as a reduced form) are only approximately rendered. The initial word "ꝏ" is a printed abbreviated form. Heading level and caput are inferred from "Cap. 17.".
